newsitem.title: GERMANY: Deutsche's Cartellieri rejects attack over Thyssen.
newsitem.headline: Deutsche's Cartellieri rejects attack over Thyssen.

text.p: Deutsche Bank AG management board member Ulrich Cartellieri on Monday rejected criticism of his role in Krupp AG's takeover bid for Thyssen AG and said he believed the bid would benefit both steel companies.

Cartellieri, who is a member of the supervisory board of Thyssen, had come under fire from employee representatives for not informing Thyssen of Krupp's impending bid even though his bank had been mandated to help Krupp arrange the takeover.

Fried. Krupp AG Hoesch-Krupp launched the bid last Tuesday but it was shelved on Wednesday for eight days of talks on a possible uncontested merger. If the talks fail, Krupp has said it will go ahead with the takeover.
In a press statement, Cartellieri said revealing the takeover bid to Thyssen ahead of time would have been "an inadmissable use of business information of third parties".
He reiterated that he was reserving the right to step down as Thyssen supervisory board member at the next supervisory board meeting on March 27.
He added that he shared the view of many experts that a merger of Thyssen and Krupp -- at least in their steel activities -- would be a good thing.
"...it would be advantageous for both companies, for the private sector restructuring and strengthening of the German steel industry and for the Ruhr region," the statement said.

Cartellieri added that only a merger of both companies could lead to the creation of an efficient industrial group by world standards and prevent the continuing loss of jobs at both Thyssen and Krupp.
"The attempt to reach this goal through a public takeover bid is legitimate. It must be possible to do so according to internationally valid rules on the German capital market as well."
Cartellieri said he had expected that both companies would hold talks ahead of the takeover bid but added that this had failed due to "indiscretions."
"I continue to hope that despite the situation that has arisen a dialogue in the spirit of partnership will lead to a coming together at least in the steel business."
